headline: Apple's smart home camera reportedly won't record video
summary: The rumored device, part of a new Apple smart home ecosystem, would use AI to analyze environments and provide text event descriptions, prioritizing user privacy over traditional video footage.
details: Apple is reportedly developing a smart home camera that will not record video footage, according to Mark Gurman. This privacy-focused device is expected to be part of a new Apple smart home ecosystem, potentially launching next month.

The camera, codenamed J450, is described as a cylindrical sensor with a very low frame rate. It uses embedded AI to analyze its environment on-device, similar to Sony IMX500 sensors, without the need to store or secure actual video.

Instead of video, the camera will provide users with text event descriptions, such as detecting when someone enters a room. While it may feature facial recognition, Gurman emphasized that there will be no video recording capability.

This approach aligns with Apple Home's existing 'Detect Activity' setting for HomeKit Secure Video, which tracks motion without streaming or recording video. The underlying technology is also reportedly similar to what Apple is developing for AirPods with cameras.
caption:

headline: GrayKey maker reportedly bypasses iPhone's 'Inactivity Reboot' security feature
summary: Magnet Forensics, the company behind GrayKey, has reportedly found a method to circumvent the 72-hour automatic reboot, potentially allowing access to data on locked iPhones.
details: Magnet Forensics, the company known for its GrayKey device, has reportedly discovered a way to bypass a key iPhone security feature. This feature automatically reboots an iPhone if it hasn't been unlocked for 72 hours, which is designed to prevent brute-force attacks on passcodes.

The alleged bypass would allow tools like GrayKey to continue attempting to unlock devices indefinitely, extending the window for forensic data extraction. This development could significantly impact the ability of law enforcement and other agencies to access data on seized iPhones.
caption:
